summary: A Fairbanks jury convicted a 58-year-old man of two counts of second-degree sexual abuse of a minor on Oct. 2, and six days later the court's public file records no verdict, no remand and no sentencing hearing; the conviction is public because the Alaska Department of Law published a release on Oct. 5. A Fourth Judicial District grand jury returned a Class A felony count of leaving the scene of an injury accident on Oct. 7, replacing a Class A misdemeanour drink-driving count on the same count of a Nenana case, and indicted three Class C felony counts in a separate Fairbanks case. A change of plea was entered on Oct. 2 in a case charging two counts of second-degree murder dated to November 1993. A man under indictment for kidnapping was arraigned in Superior Court and released to a third-party custodian. Two more case numbers printed by the court no longer appear in its public database, one of them the court number for a Nenana assault arrest on Oct. 7. The filings counts below are the court report's own counts for the week ending Oct. 7; that report lists a Nenana case number that the court's public database does not return, and it revised a row it had printed as carrying no charge into a Class C felony.

entries.title: Fairbanks jury convicts man of two counts of second-degree sexual abuse of a minor
body: A Fairbanks jury found Donald Dittman, 58, guilty of two counts of sexual abuse of a minor in the second degree on Friday, Oct. 2, the Alaska Department of Law announced in a release dated Oct. 5.

The case is 4FA-24-02136CR, filed in November 2024. Alaska CourtView records two counts, both sexual abuse of a minor in the second degree, contact, AS 11.41.436(a)(3), Class B felonies, both offence-dated June 20, 2024 at Fairbanks and both recorded as domestic violence related. Both counts were indicted in December 2024.

The Department of Law release states that the person abused was a family member, that the conduct was reported four days after it occurred, that Dittman was remanded into the custody of the Department of Corrections and is held without bail, and that he faces 20 to 35 years on each count. A sentencing hearing is scheduled for March 18, 2027.

The court's public file records a jury trial on each of five days from Sep. 28 to Oct. 2 and no result against it. Its most recent docket entry is dated Oct. 2 and is the jury instructions. The file records no verdict, no remand and no sentencing hearing.

The release states that the case was prosecuted by Assistant District Attorney Lauren Wood and that the Fairbanks Police Department conducted the investigation. The person abused is not named in the release and is not named here.

entries.title: Grand jury returns a Class A felony count in a Parks Highway collision case, replacing a misdemeanour
body: A Fourth Judicial District grand jury returned an indictment on Wednesday, Oct. 7 in 4NE-26-00097CR, State of Alaska vs. Chambers, Jennifer Sara, a case filed at the Nenana court on Sep. 28 over a collision at mile 318 of the Parks Highway on Sep. 27.

Alaska CourtView records that one count was originally charged as driving under the influence, AS 28.35.030(a)(1), a Class A misdemeanour, and that the indicted charge against that same count reads leaving the scene of an accident and failing to assist in an injury accident, AS 28.35.060(c), a Class A felony, with a stage date of Oct. 7.

A second count, assault in the third degree, cause injury with a weapon, AS 11.41.220(a)(1)(B), a Class C felony, was indicted unchanged. A third count of driving under the influence, a Class A misdemeanour, carries no indicted charge.

The docket records the indictment filed in Superior Court with jurisdiction transferred, the indictment filed in open court, an information adding a misdemeanour count to the indictment, and a felony pre-trial order effective Oct. 28. Bail was recorded on Oct. 6 at $2,500. A preliminary hearing remained on the event list for Oct. 8 with no result recorded.
She is charged, not convicted. Nothing in the court record describes the incident or identifies anyone recorded as a victim.

entries.title: Three Class C felony counts indicted in a Fairbanks vehicle theft and forgery case
body: The same grand jury returned an indictment on Oct. 7 in 4FA-26-01980CR, State of Alaska vs. Wallace, Madisyn Jane, filed Sep. 30 over offences recorded on Sep. 28 at Fairbanks.

All three felony counts now carry an indicted charge: vehicle theft in the first degree, AS 11.46.360(a)(1); forgery in the second degree, AS 11.46.505(a)(1); and forging or altering an assignment of title or security interest, AS 28.10.491(a)(2). All three are Class C felonies. A fourth count of violating conditions of release for a misdemeanour, a Class B misdemeanour, carries no indicted charge.

The docket records the indictment filed in Superior Court with jurisdiction transferred, the indictment filed in open court, an information adding a misdemeanour count, and a felony pre-trial order effective Oct. 14. Preliminary hearings that had stood for Oct. 8 and Oct. 20 are vacated.
She is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Change of plea entered in a Fairbanks case charging two 1993 murder counts
body: A change of plea hearing was held on Friday, Oct. 2 at 11:30 a.m. in Courtroom 404 of the Fairbanks courthouse in 4FA-25-02251CR, State of Alaska vs. Popps, Christopher M.

Alaska CourtView records two counts, both unclassified felonies, both offence-dated Nov. 22, 1993 at Fairbanks: murder in the second degree, extreme indifference, AS 11.41.110(a)(2), and murder in the second degree, intend serious injury, AS 11.41.110(a)(1). Both counts were indicted on June 25, 2026. The case was filed in November 2025.

The docket records a waiver of indictment filed on Oct. 2, log notes for the change of plea, and a court order for a presentence report entered Oct. 5. A scheduled trial week of Oct. 12 is vacated and a sentencing hearing is set for March 23, 2027 at 2:45 p.m. The file does not record what plea was entered or to which counts, and no amended charge appears on either count.

The Fairbanks Daily News-Miner reported on Oct. 7 that Christopher Popps, 54, of Michigan, pleaded guilty to reduced charges of criminally negligent homicide and tampering with physical evidence, that he faces up to 10 years, that he was indicted after human remains were found inside a barrel near mile 47 of the Steese Highway in May 2025, and that troopers identified him after receiving an anonymous tip in January 2025. Those reduced counts do not appear on the public court file.

entries.title: Fairbanks man charged with felony assault after an Adams Drive arrest
body: Daniel Owen Knight, 28, was arrested at the 3200 block of Adams Drive at 11:20 on Tuesday, Oct. 6, the Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin records, on a charge the department records as assault in the third degree, cause fear of injury with a weapon, a felony. The same case number carries an incident the department classifies as aggravated assault with a cutting instrument at the 1600 block of Washington Drive at 10:39 the same morning.

The court file, 4FA-26-02028CR, carries one count of assault in the third degree, cause fear of injury with a weapon, AS 11.41.220(a)(1)(A), a Class C felony, offence-dated Oct. 6 at Fairbanks and not recorded as domestic violence related. The count is on a complaint and has not been to a grand jury.

He was arraigned on Oct. 7 at 1:30 p.m. in Courtroom 102, counsel was appointed from the bench and a temporary order with release conditions was entered. Preliminary hearings are set for Oct. 15 and Oct. 27.
He is charged, not convicted. When the court file was read on the morning of Oct. 7 it carried no charge and no docket entry of any kind.

entries.title: Man under indictment for kidnapping arraigned in Superior Court and released to a third-party custodian
body: A Superior Court arraignment and a bail hearing were both held on Wednesday, Oct. 7 at 10:00 a.m. in Courtroom 402 before Judge Brent Bennett in 4FA-26-01890CR, State of Alaska vs. Claxton, Dante Nathaniel Larry.
The docket records an order and conditions of release, a third-party custodian agreement and acknowledgement, and log notes for the arraignment, all dated Oct. 7.

The file carries three counts, all offence-dated Sep. 22 and all recorded as domestic violence related: kidnapping, injury or sexual assault, AS 11.41.300(a)(1)(C), an unclassified felony, at North Pole, which a grand jury indicted on Oct. 1; and assault in the fourth degree and interference with a report of a domestic violence crime, both Class A misdemeanours, at Fairbanks.
An omnibus hearing is set for Nov. 5 and a trial week for Nov. 23. He is charged, not convicted. Nothing in the court record describes the incident or identifies anyone recorded as a victim.

entries.title: Woman arrested at Nenana on a fourth-degree assault charge
body: Troopers responded to Front Street in Nenana at about 01:25 on Wednesday, Oct. 7 for a report of a disturbance, the Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch records. The dispatch states that the investigation showed Tanna Fairbanks, 40, of Nenana, assaulted a family member causing injury, and that she was arrested for assault in the fourth degree, transported to the Fairbanks Correctional Center and held without bail.

The Alaska Court System's weekly charges report lists a case number for the arrest, 4NE-26-00100CR, filed Oct. 7 at the Nenana court with one count recorded as charging document pending or not filed. The case number returns no records in Alaska CourtView, so no charge class can be stated.
She is arrested, not convicted. Nothing in the record identifies anyone recorded as a victim.

entries.title: Man arrested at Nenana on an outstanding warrant
body: Troopers responded to a residence near Front Street in Nenana at about 01:23 on Wednesday, Oct. 7 for a report of a disturbance and contacted Anthony Wright, 40, of Nenana, the Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch records. The dispatch states that the investigation showed he had an outstanding warrant for failure to appear on an original charge of driving with a revoked licence, and that he was arrested on the warrant.

No 2026 criminal case under that name appears in Alaska CourtView on a search of files dated Sep. 1 to Oct. 8. The two Nenana dispatch entries from that morning describe the same street seven minutes apart; neither record states a connection between them.

entries.title: Man remanded to the Fairbanks jail after an assault reported outside Tanana
body: Troopers in Fairbanks received a report of an assault outside Tanana at about 18:43 on Saturday, Oct. 4, the Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch records. The dispatch states that the investigation revealed Russell Moses, 41, assaulted multiple family members in the presence of children, and that he was remanded to the Fairbanks Correctional Center on charges relating to assault in the fourth degree and assault in the presence of a child. The entry was posted on Oct. 7.
Tanana is about 130 air miles west of Fairbanks and outside this record's coverage area; the item is carried because the remand was to the Fairbanks jail and is labelled accordingly.

No court file appears in Alaska CourtView on a search of files dated Sep. 1 to Oct. 8, so no charge class can be stated. He is arrested, not convicted. Nothing in the record identifies anyone recorded as a victim, or any child.

entries.title: Six cases filed at Fairbanks on Oct. 7, four of them arraigned the same afternoon
body: Six criminal cases were filed at the Fairbanks court on Wednesday, Oct. 7. Four were arraigned at 1:30 p.m. the same day and two carry no charging document.

4FA-26-02031CR, Morry, Miranda A, carries one count of giving false information or a false report, identification when cited or served with a warrant, AS 11.56.800(a)(1)(B)(ii), a Class A misdemeanour, and one count of violating conditions of release for a misdemeanour, a Class B misdemeanour, both offence-dated Oct. 7 at Fairbanks. It is the court file for a police arrest at the 1900 block of Mary Ann Street at 01:13 that morning.

4FA-26-02032CR, Semaken, Jerome Benjamine, carries one count of criminal trespass in the first degree, in a dwelling, AS 11.46.320(a)(2), a Class A misdemeanour, recorded as domestic violence related, offence-dated Oct. 7 at Fairbanks. It is the court file for a police arrest at the 1600 block of Stacia Street at 03:30 that morning.

4FA-26-02033CR, Ahyakak-Clerc, Sebastien Burnell, carries reckless driving, leaving an accident without providing information and reckless endangerment, the last a Class A misdemeanour, all offence-dated Oct. 7 at Fairbanks. The case appears in no police bulletin or trooper dispatch entry.

4FA-26-02034CR, Griswold, Arthur Ervin, carries one count of driving with a licence cancelled, suspended or revoked with a prior conviction, AS 28.15.291(a)(2), a Class A misdemeanour, offence-dated Sep. 2 at North Pole. No hearing is calendared.

4FA-26-02029CR, Sarten, Ishi Santana, and 4FA-26-02030CR, Maple, Thomas Monroe, each carry one count recorded as charging document pending or not filed, with no charge class on the file. They are the court numbers for police arrests at the 1600 block of East Cowles Street at 21:40 on Oct. 6, recorded by police as indecent exposure in the second degree, and at the 900 block of Twenty-Third Avenue at Turner Street at 00:59 on Oct. 7, recorded by police as driving under the influence with a breath alcohol level of .08 or over and driving with a licence cancelled, suspended or revoked. Both are set for arraignment on Oct. 13.
All are charged or arrested, not convicted.

entries.title: Two days the police bulletin had reported as holding nothing now hold eight events each
body: The Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin returned no events for Tuesday, Oct. 6 when it was read on the mornings of Oct. 6 and Oct. 7, the second reading a day after the day had ended, and returned no events for Wednesday, Oct. 7 when it was read on the morning of Oct. 7.

Read on the morning of Oct. 8, the bulletin holds eight events for Oct. 6 and eight for Oct. 7. Among them are the felony assault arrest at the 3200 block of Adams Drive and the aggravated assault incident recorded under the same case number, both carried above; three arrests on Oct. 7 that now have court files; and two arrests on Oct. 7 that do not.
Monday, Oct. 5 has gone from five events to nine and Sunday, Oct. 4 from one to two. None of the six additions to those two days is an arrest.
Counts taken from this feed are a floor established at the moment of reading and not a total for the day.

entries.title: Two more case numbers printed by the court no longer appear in the court's public database
body: Eleven case numbers that appear in the Alaska Court System's own published reports return no records in Alaska CourtView when searched by case number. Two of the eleven stopped resolving overnight.

4FA-26-02008CR, Anderson, Vernon Gerald, was filed Oct. 3 with one count recorded as charging document pending or not filed and an arraignment set for Oct. 9. The file was read on each of the mornings of Oct. 4 to Oct. 7 and returned no records on the morning of Oct. 8, by case number and on a search of files dated Sep. 1 to Oct. 8.
4NE-26-00100CR, printed by the court's weekly charges report under Wednesday, Oct. 7, has never resolved. It is the court number for the Nenana assault arrest carried above.

Eight of the eleven appear in the court's own criminal dispositions report as closed cases, with their closing dates. Three do not: the two above and 4FA-26-02006CR, which carried three filed Class A misdemeanour counts when it was read on Oct. 3. The dispositions report's window closes on Oct. 5, so a closure after that date could not appear in it.
No explanation for any of the eleven appears in any public record this report can reach.

entries.title: The court's weekly filings report added no cases to past days this week, but revised a row it had printed
body: The Alaska Court System's weekly criminal charges report for Oct. 1 to Oct. 7, run at 9:01 p.m. on Oct. 7, lists 49 cases at Fairbanks, three at Nenana, two at Delta Junction and none at Healy. Wednesday, Sep. 30 and its 11 Fairbanks cases have left the rolling seven-day window.
For the first time since the run of Oct. 3, the report has not added a case to a filing day it had already published. Every carried-over day holds exactly what it held in the previous run.

One row it had printed has changed. The run of Oct. 6 listed 4FA-26-02028CR under Tuesday, Oct. 6 with one count recorded as charging document pending or not filed. The run of Oct. 7 lists the same case number under the same day with one count of assault in the third degree, a Class C felony. The day's total is three cases in both runs.
The counts in the filings section of this report are the court report's own counts for its stated window.

The new count is violating conditions of release for a misdemeanour, AS 11.56.757(a)(misdB), a Class B misdemeanour, offence-dated Oct. 6 at Fairbanks and not recorded as domestic violence related. An arraignment was held on Oct. 7 at 1:30 p.m., counsel was entered and a temporary order with release conditions was entered. A bail hearing is set for Oct. 12 at 10:00 a.m. The event list records the arraignments of Oct. 4 and Oct. 5 as continued.

A pre-trial conference is set for Dec. 3 and a trial week for Dec. 14. She is charged, not convicted.
